title: Regular pullback of dimension functions by fibre local dimension
statement: Let $r:P\to X$ be a regular morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes [def-exc-excellent-ring], meaning flat with fibres that remain regular after every finite residue-field extension [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $\delta_X:|X|\to\mathbf Z$ be a dimension function: its value drops by one along every immediate geometric specialization, where immediate means codimension one in the strict localization [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $b_r(u)=\dim\mathcal O_{P_{r(u)},u}$. Then the function $\delta_P:|P|\to\mathbf Z$ defined by $\delta_P(u)=\delta_X(r(u))-b_r(u)$ is a dimension function on $P$. No finite-type or finite-presentation hypothesis on $r$ is imposed.

source.place: Expose XIV, Proposition 2.5.4, printed pp.217–218: regular pullback of dimension functions.

mathlib_searches.query: Regular morphisms of excellent schemes pull back a dimension function by subtracting the local dimension of the fibre
If f is a regular morphism of excellent schemes and delta is a dimension function then delta f y minus dimension of local fibre at y is a dimension function
